prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, in which ligand design made the construction of aryl amines routine

statement.case_for: I keep Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling as the whole prize. It is the one candidate on the shortlist where all three of my tests are met at once: the structural and mechanistic picture of the catalyst is established (oxidative addition, amine binding and deprotonation, then reductive elimination from a Pd-amido complex), the method is used daily across discovery, process and materials chemistry, and the attribution is clean at two names. Answering the chair directly, the new chemical principle beyond the 2010 prize is ligand control of C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes, with bulky, electron-rich phosphines and carbenes suppressing the competing beta-hydride elimination. That is a different bond-forming step with a different failure mode from C-C coupling, and it required its own ligand families, not a transfer of the earlier ones. More than twenty-five years of independent confirmation remove any maturity question.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize honoured Pd cross-coupling, and a colleague can fairly say that C-N coupling shares the Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold and is a heteroatom extension. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a real precedent and has to be placed in the citation or background text. A single method prize is also the quietest story for the public next to base editing or degraders, and a prize judged by enablement is easy to dismiss as overdue housekeeping. Finally, a one-part prize concentrates the committee's risk on a single novelty argument.

responses.point: Somfai pairs B002 with Liu alone for base editing, to avoid a one-topic prize and to give the committee a second, distinct achievement within the three-name cap.
responses.response: Liu alone does remove my round-1 objection to trainee-led credit, and the TadA point is a real chemical addition to the 2020 prize. I still do not add it. The two parts share nothing, and the pairing is justified mainly by hedging the novelty doubt about B002, not by a common idea. Base editing also arrives four to six years after CRISPR, with clinical outcomes still early and the Nishida and Kondo claim open. I would rather defend B002 on the ligand-control answer you and I now agree on than attach a part whose own attribution is contested. I accept that B029 is my first alternative.

responses.point: Chabes pairs base editing (Liu) with PROTAC degradation (Crews and Deshaies) as the two best-supported ideas, each with a clean one- or two-name citation.
responses.response: I agree both are genuine concepts and that the Liu-only wording is the cleanest base-editing attribution. My difficulty is the evidence threshold. Neither part has a regulatory approval behind it, and you yourself say clinical benefit for degraders is unproven and that the cereblon strand is left outside. A prize for ideas whose payoff is still pending is a bet on timing. For me a stated threshold would be a first approved degrader or a clearly positive late-stage readout. Until then B002 is the better-settled case, and I keep B018 as an alternative, not a part.

responses.point: Aqvist holds degradation as the whole prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and is open to swapping Handa for Ciulli.
responses.response: The ternary-complex cooperativity and structure-guided linker work are the part I find most convincing, and Ciulli's VHL ligand structures are the strongest crystallographic contribution in the field, so I would rank him ahead of Handa if the citation is the PROTAC concept. I do not think one citation can honestly cover both the PROTAC and cereblon strands, as Somfai also says: cereblon identification is target identification and belongs to a separate part. Because that would exceed three names, I do not see a defensible three-person B018 today, which is another reason I do not move it ahead of B002.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, asks whether Somfai and Zou can state the new principle in B002, and whether B002 would then enter his configuration, since he wants a mature partner for base editing.
responses.response: The principle is ligand-controlled reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes against beta-hydride elimination, and it can be stated in one sentence to a general audience as making the bond between nitrogen and carbon in aromatic rings routine. If you want the mature partner for B029 that you described to Somfai, B002 with Liu is a three-name configuration that fits the cap. I would not make it my own, but I would not oppose it, and I would rather see that pairing than a two-part prize built on a degrader not yet approved.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the ligand-control argument as a distinct achievement from the 2010 cross-coupling prize
Whether the Kosugi precedent is best handled in the citation or in background text
Whether a single method prize can win a majority against the two-part base-editing configurations, and whether any majority of five forms at all
Whether a first approved degrader will arrive soon enough to change the ranking of B018
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. None of the credited names for B002, B029 or B018 are collaborators, mentors or Stockholm University colleagues. My only general tie is an interest in crystallographic methods, relevant most to B019 and not part of my position, and I share a Stockholm University affiliation with the Secretary, which involves no credited name.
